clicking a party member's figure (x below 60) opens member_sheet in the original; there is no character sheet yet.
the exit transition root 047C:1320(6, 0, 0, 0) is not reproduced.

the original reads SAVES\DEFAULT here too (R037+0x4184, the open not checked; see D-66e575 for Quickstart); without the file it reads through an unset handle, and the 483.07 notes say characters can then not be created. Here the ready-made characters come with the game (DefaultParty), so the file is not needed.
a new member's row shows the shield of its record, where the menu loads PICS\SHIELDA.PIC until H is pressed.
the original advances the bubble every 0x5DD passes of its polling loop (machine speed); here every 6 frames (about 100 ms).
the exit transition root 047C:1320(6, 0, 0, 0) is not reproduced.

the pointer does not change to the hand pictures (handicon, handicn2) over lists; the menu bar (menu_bar_run) comes with GameUi.Poll (MenuBar), its Alt keys through MenuBarKey; its party_icons_dirty redraw is not needed.
the combat branch (DS:907A == 1 and the member on floor 0x9D: thunk 09C0:1D51) is not reached: battles do not open the sheet yet.
the original readies or unreadies the line's stack without checking it exists (an empty pack reads past its end); here nothing happens.
as for A and U, a line past the pack's end is ignored (the original reads its code).
Ctrl-F1 makes to −1, which the original reads as the record before member 0; here nothing is given.

the original reads party[(key & 0xF) + 11] (records past the five members, normally not "able"), draws member frame 12..16 from past the frame table and redraws the sheet; here the sheet is redrawn only.
the original redraws only panel row k − 12 (party_panel_frames(k − 12)); here the whole panel.

the original streams the file through a ring buffer while a timer interrupt shows the cels; here the decoded frames are shown one by one at their ticks. A key press stops the READING in the original (kbhit() in the loop of 0150) while the cels already read still play out, and the key stays in the buffer so the next animation's reading stops at once too; a skip here cuts the current animation short immediately (the one difference) and the later ones follow the original: they are not shown, but their music cues still play.
the original reads the whole file (or a full ring buffer) before the first cel; its time depends on the machine. The opening uses the measured times (OpeningTiming).
cards_shutdown's files (charactr.tmp, locs.tmp, events.tmp) and frees are not needed; only its sound_play(1) is played.
the original ends the program when the card loop ends (the 0x62 or -0x63 screen): it frees its buffers and exits to DOS; here the player comes back to the start screen, where Alt-Q leaves.
copyprot_run_vec asks the copy-protection question (a code from the manual); it is not asked here. The event it leaves behind, for 0x3E80 hours (about 22 months), is created as in the original.
the game returns to the start screen instead of exiting to DOS; cards_shutdown and cards_startup's reloads are not needed.
the wrapper's card-picture redraw afterwards (thunk 09C0:1EA5) is the card screen's job here.
the original redraws the card afterwards (thunk 09C0:1EA5); here the screen as it was is put back.
the game leaves through an exception that unwinds to DarklandsGame.Run (nothing to shut down on a PC host, no dk.tmp)
the original exits to DOS (exit_) after the death film; here the player comes back to the start screen.

the original polls: a loop tests key_pressed(), mouse_buttons (bit 1 left, 2 right, held) and the click counter itself; this record is one event of an edge-triggered queue, so a button held across screens produces one PlayerAction, not many.

waits sleep 16 ms per frame instead of spinning; the pointer (the COMMONSP.IMG gauntlet) is drawn into a copy of the screen (the original draws the mouse cursor through the driver); F12 saves a screenshot (host feature).

the host reports the buttons once a frame; a release is counted when a frame sees the button up after one that saw it down, at the pointer's place in that frame (the hosts keep a click within one frame for a frame).

`stop` (StopAtFirstOption), `init` (the hotspot table reset) and `icon` (the drop cap) are the C's parameters; init is always on here. The original draws a character with the driver's char_width/gfx_text (asm); the glyph widths come from the font file here (TextPainter.Advance), so a byte the font lacks counts as width 0.

measured by running the drawing layout on a scratch screen instead of a second copy of the loop; the C's copy has one difference: it does not track conditional passages (0x01 .. 0x13) and counts the bytes of a skipped option line differently, which the texts measured (hints, short messages) do not contain.

the original cuts the 26 pictures once at start-up into DOS memory; here they are cut on first use. A letter outside A..Z, or a missing ILLMCAPS.PIC, draws the plain character (the original has no such case: a first byte outside '@'..'[' is not a drop cap).

the original has no global handler for F1..F5/Ctrl-F: the card engine and the map each handle them in their own loops (and only while they wait); this one applies them in every wait of GameUi.Poll. The original also guards Alt-O, Alt-S, Alt-L and F6 with the screen flags DS:9893, DS:9920, DS:9934 and DS:987F (set 1 by screens that allow the operation, 0 elsewhere, e.g. no saving in a battle); here only the inn's roster sets DS:9920 / DS:9934 (SaveGameItem, LoadGameItem), and the operations are otherwise allowed where the host supplies the action.
in the open country the original indexes locations[-1] (cur_loc −1); the screen does not open here.
root 0000:0000 is GameUi.Poll's (MenuBar, HotKeys).
the original shows sheets while member_sheet_vec returns another member (row != -1); IGameScreens.CharacterSheet returns nothing, so one sheet is shown.
the pointer stays visible (the host's pointer has no hide count).
after "no" the button picture is still drawn when pressed.
root 0000:0000 is GameUi.Poll's (MenuBar, HotKeys).
rows past the pile's end are ignored (see LootSharing.Get).

a member whose combat floor (cbt_floor, DS:A6B4) is −99 (he left the battlefield through an exit) is skipped after thunk 09C0:1D51 = R022+0x04E4 is called for him (asm 0DB4..0DC8: DS:8DC4 = slot first); this screen does not see the battle's combatant floors, so the test is absent (in a battle it belongs with the R022 work of the battle branch).
the original loops forever when no member qualifies; here the search stops after five slots.
the original redraws the picture without set_palette; the picture's colours are applied here.

with the battle's move mode at 2 (single file: DS:C102 as the last battle left it) the original then sets the battlefield's members walking after each other (thunk 09C0:1DE7, R016+0x0E7E) on the last battle's records; outside a battle that is not done here.
the "Show Changes" tick follows the option; the original's tick keeps its last toggle across a load (the load sets the music, sound and difficulty ticks only).
Right with no item chosen reads items[-1].sub (memory before the item table); here that is "no sub-menu".
empty here).

the original draws into off-screen buffers and copies a 260x184 window; it keeps the party as view-relative registers and scrolls the view in jumps of 128 pixels across and 92 down when the marker comes within 20 pixels of an edge (Scroll below follows those jumps and thresholds). Here the screen redraws the visible tiles every frame from absolute positions.

not ported from the loop: the joystick (DS:0880..DS:0882, DS:E3FA/DS:E3FB), the "party_icons_dirty" reload after the menu bar (the bar itself, right button and F10, comes with GameUi.Poll), and the copy-protection check of overland_map (the card engine side, see DarklandsGame.Travel).
the portrait click opens the sheet once per press (the original would reopen it every pass while the button stays down); the steering follows the held button as in the original.
the original looks at the key buffer only after the delays; here a key ends the delay at once.

the original also moves its row buffer by 0x41 rows at a time (1dd4 reloading map rows) and corrects the marker at the map's borders with its own arithmetic (including a factor 5 on the vertical correction); here the view is clamped to the map (ClampOrigin).
a message number past the end of the file shows an empty box.
party_info_close (R034+0x119C) marks the party icons for redrawing; here GameScreens2 puts the earlier screen back.
the original also moves the mouse pointer onto the town (mouse_move); the host owns the pointer here.

the status texts that replace the bars while a member is "away" is drawn only as bars here (see Draw); the combat extras of member_bars (the carried member's bars, the status-letter column of member_status_letter root 0000:18FA) belong to battles (BattleScreen.DrawPanel).
the original copies each finished row from the off-screen page to the screen (copy_rect_clipped) and hides the mouse while it does; here it is drawn straight into the screen.
the value is printed without the thousands comma itoa_commas would add (the values stay below 1000).
the exit transition (root 047C:1320 with 6, 0, 0, 0) is not reproduced; the screen is put back as it was before the card's own redraw (thunk 09C0:1EA5, ICardScreen.Reload).
F1..F5 open the character sheets here (HotKeys' divergence); the original's handler gets them as unknown keys.
a row past the figure list names a picture that does not exist (the original's picture load fails); nothing is drawn.

the original redraws the whole screen when a hot key's box asks for it (DS:9C46); here the hot keys put back what they cover themselves. Alt-Q is the game-wide hot key (the screen's own 0x1000 case, saint_finish then quit, is not reached).
the success message comes after the help here (the help's own change reports, when "saintly changes" is on, therefore come first); the original shows it before.
root 0000:0000 is GameUi.Poll's (MenuBar, HotKeys); the party_icons_dirty redraw is not modelled.
the "Saving Game" box of a save in a battle is drawn in colour 9 by the original; it has the box's own colour here.
the original runs the start screen once and ends the program when the game ends (the main loop returns, free_buffer, exit); DarklandsGame.Run comes back to this screen after a game instead.
the original starts the chosen action as the pressed button is drawn, with no pause (loading takes the time); the 150 ms here only lets the press be seen.
after "no" the screen simply goes on.

the EMS check always passes: there is no expanded memory to lack. DORMANT: "Unable to find EMS memory\n" and exit(0); "Darklands requires at least 176K of EMS memory free." (BANNER.DAT entry 19) when fewer than 11 pages are free (R000+0x1150); the EMS error texts of R000+0x0000.
no Ctrl-Break here.

there is no DOS memory here: the program's block is its EXE's load size (header) plus its minimum allocation and the PSP, the free memory a constant; the check always passes, the -O figures are an estimate. dk.tmp is not written.
the files are only looked for here; the game reads them when it needs them.
the original returns to DOS with its message on the screen; here the screen stays until a key, a click or the window is closed.
that 0 -> 5 -> 0 recolouring is not repeated (it changes at most colour-5 pixels of the card behind).
the original waits for the vertical retrace before reprogramming the timer and re-syncs to it every 70 frames (047C:026A..0284); here the timer is exact and never drifts.

the original only knows the files of CONFIG.DRK's letter; the GOG release keeps the FM drivers as .DC/.DB (renamed for the dual-board setup), so a choice is found by the driver's name rather than its file name.
cards 1 (Covox) and 3 (early SB Pro) are played as a Sound Blaster, 5 and 6 (Pro Audio Spectrum, Gold) as a later SB Pro: the drivers' code for those cards' own mixers is not emulated.

the game loads the file when the opening or ending starts and frees it afterwards (without telling the driver); here the driver is restarted with the file when a piece needs a file other than the one it has, and the file stays in the emulated memory.
requests still waiting for their tick are carried out first, earlier by at most the output's latency.
the game swaps when a battle starts and ends, whatever is played; here the swap happens at the first effect (battle driver) or music (towns driver) request after the change.

the VGA's own ROM font is not part of the game; a host can load an 8×16 BIOS font dump (TextFont.Load), else the built-in TextFont.Fallback draws the characters (same cell layout, other glyph shapes).
